READING

**Deadlines and sequencing**

Three dates cluster together. Faskally's free hold on Culverstone expires 2026-12-05, after which a £40,000 non-refundable deposit preserves it to 2028-06-30. The Hallowbrand landlord wants an answer by 2026-12-19. Planning was validated 2026-08-14, eleven days ago.

Under KESTERWICK the sequence is: pay Faskally before 5 December, let Hallowbrand go before 19 December. The fourteen days between those two dates form a natural last checkpoint — the deposit is paid, the option is secured, and Hallowbrand has not yet lapsed. Once 19 December passes without renewing, the position is irreversible.

---

**Planning timeline scenarios**

Working from the validated date of 2026-08-14:

| Scenario | Consent | Works complete (+22 wks) | Hallowbrand ends | Time at Nethercote |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 13-week target | ~2026-11-13 | ~2027-04-16 | 2027-11-30 | None — Culverstone ready seven months early |
| 34-week median | ~2027-04-09 | ~2027-09-11 | 2027-11-30 | None — 2½ months early |
| 61-week worst | ~2027-10-14 | ~2028-03-16 | 2027-11-30 | ~3½ months, ~£64,750 |

The median — the authority's own recorded midpoint over three years — produces Culverstone opening around 3 September, approximately ten days before the bid deadline of 14 September 2027. The slowest determination ever recorded produces roughly 3½ months at Nethercote after the Hallowbrand lease expires. Crucially, in every scenario the new 44/44A contract (starting 2028-04-01) begins after Culverstone would be open.

---

**The rent arithmetic**

Annual rent:

- ARDENSHAW: £214,000
- KESTERWICK: £118,000
- Differential: £96,000 per year

Over ten years the ARDENSHAW rent bill is £2,140,000. Over ten years from Culverstone occupation the rent bill is £1,180,000. Gross saving in Trentmoor's favour: **£960,000**.

---

**Dead mileage cost (Culverstone only)**

Culverstone is 3 miles further from the Verrancombe Bridge stand. Each of 22 vehicles travels that distance twice per operating day.

22 × 6 miles × 313 days × £0.63 = **£26,029 per year**

Net annual advantage of KESTERWICK over ARDENSHAW: £96,000 − £26,029 = **£69,971**.

---

**Full cost comparison — worst historical case**

| KESTERWICK cost item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Works | £480,000 |
| Faskally deposit | £40,000 |
| Nethercote (3½ months) | £64,750 |
| Dead mileage over 10 years | £260,290 |
| **Total extra cost** | **£845,040** |

Against £960,000 of rent saving, KESTERWICK still comes out **£114,960 ahead** even under the slowest determination the authority has ever recorded. Under the median scenario (no Nethercote) the advantage widens to **£179,710**.

---

**Works payback**

At £96,000/year gross saving, the £520,000 of upfront spend (works plus deposit) is recovered in 5 years 5 months. After dead mileage the net saving is £69,971/year and recovery takes approximately 7 years 5 months — inside the ten-year term, with two and a half years of clear advantage remaining.

---

**Cash and liquidity**

Starting position: £640,000 cash + £200,000 undrawn facility = £840,000.

After the £40,000 December deposit: £800,000 available.

In the worst case, works payments run from around October 2027 to March 2028 (22 weeks), simultaneously with Nethercote rent. Total peak demand: approximately £544,750. Construction is staged, not paid on day one. Between the deposit date and the start of works there are roughly 14 months in which the business continues to trade and generate cash. The liquidity position is tight in the worst case but does not require drawing the full facility and does not require the business to post a zero operating surplus. It is manageable.

Under ARDENSHAW, no works are needed and no deposit is paid, but from December 2027 the annual rent bill is £214,000 — £73,000 more per year than the current Hallowbrand commitment — and that pressure compounds for a decade.

---

**The 2027-09-14 bid**

Depot cost enters the bid as a fixed line. Consider each path:

*ARDENSHAW:* The number is £214,000 and certain from the moment of signing. It is certain because it is large. Any competitor depoting at a comparable or lower cost can undercut Trentmoor on this line alone.

*KESTERWICK, median case:* The depot cost is approximately £118,000 + £26,029 dead mileage = £144,029. At bid date Culverstone is open or days away from opening. The number is competitive and certain.

*KESTERWICK, worst case:* At 14 September 2027, planning has not yet been determined (consent expected mid-October). Works would complete approximately 16 March 2028, before the new contract starts 1 April 2028. The bid can be priced at Culverstone costs with high confidence, but not absolute certainty, because the sole remaining risk is outright refusal rather than further delay. That is the residual exposure examined below.

---

**Risk: planning refusal**

Delay is already priced into the worst-case calculation above, and KESTERWICK still wins. The scenario that makes ARDENSHAW preferable is outright refusal. Refusal would mean: £40,000 deposit gone, Hallowbrand renewal lapsed, Trentmoor on Nethercote with no workshop seeking a depot at whatever terms the market offers. That is a genuinely bad position.

The factors that bear on refusal probability:

1. The application has been validated — the authority has confirmed it is properly constituted.
2. The site is being held by Faskally specifically for a coach operator's use; the landlord and its advisers presumably assessed viability before committing to the option arrangement.
3. The tendering authority for the 44/44A is Verrancombe County. The planning authority is also Verrancombe County. A bus depot serving a county-tendered network is unlikely to meet active resistance from the same county.
4. The Faskally deposit holds the site to June 2028 — even the worst recorded determination (October 2027) plus works (March 2028) clears that deadline.

None of this makes refusal impossible. If management has specific grounds to believe refusal is probable — neighbouring objections, site designation issues, political context — that changes the calculus materially and ARDENSHAW becomes the safer call. Absent that, the refusal risk on a validated depot application at a site held for this purpose reads as a low-probability tail risk, not a central scenario.

---

**Comparative position in 2037**

Under ARDENSHAW, in November 2037 Trentmoor faces another lease renegotiation with a landlord who has already demonstrated willingness to increase from £141,000 to £214,000 (a 52% uplift in one cycle). Under KESTERWICK, a 2038 renegotiation at Culverstone is with a landlord whose site is equipped with hardstanding, a fuel island and a two-bay workshop — improvements Trentmoor paid for, but also improvements that make the site worth more to any operator. Neither position is obviously stronger a decade out, but ARDENSHAW compounds the landlord's leverage.

---

**Judgment**

The financial arithmetic is clear across every planning scenario. The dead mileage cost is real and must be carried every year the 44/44A network runs from Culverstone, but it does not come close to erasing the rent differential. The works cost is substantial and is paid into land Trentmoor does not own, but it pays back inside the lease term. The bid in September 2027 is priced more competitively from Culverstone in all scenarios except outright refusal, which is the one risk that is genuinely unquantifiable but appears low given the validated application and the alignment of planning and tendering authority.

ARDENSHAW's case rests on certainty — known cost, workshop from day one, no planning exposure, clean bid. It is a coherent position. It is also £96,000 a year more expensive for a decade, meaning Trentmoor pays roughly £960,000 for that certainty, receives no workshop it could not have built for £480,000, and enters 2037 still wholly dependent on a landlord with demonstrated pricing power. The price of ARDENSHAW's certainty is too high relative to the risks KESTERWICK actually carries.

CALL
KESTERWICK

GROUNDS
The ten-year rent saving of £960,000 over ARDENSHAW exceeds every foreseeable KESTERWICK cost — works, deposit, worst-case Nethercote, and a full decade of dead mileage — by more than £114,000 even on the slowest planning determination the authority has ever recorded, and Culverstone also enters the September 2027 bid at roughly £70,000 per year lower depot cost than Hallowbrand would, with the only scenario favouring ARDENSHAW being outright planning refusal on a validated application at a site held by its landlord specifically for this use.
